text:
oliver: Drafted a doc PR that explains airgap image layering (split runtime vs payload images) and a recommended cert migration for HSM-backed installs. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4680 - PTAL.

maya: Love the image layering callout. Can we add an example manifest format that lists image SHA digests alongside local filenames so operators can map them offline?

oliver: Added a tiny manifest example:

```
# images.manifest
sha256:abcd1234... runtime-images.tar.gz
sha256:ffee9876... payload-images-v2.tar.gz
```

ben: HSM cert migration note: include steps to export and wrap the HSM PKCS#11 config into the airgap bundle and a safety check: `pkcs11-tool --login --list-objects` to confirm keys are present before cutover. Also suggest backing up /var/lib/pkcs11 and encrypting with customer key.

sara: I added a short systemd snippet recommendation for delayed HSM probe: `ExecStartPost=/bin/sh -c 'sleep 8; /usr/local/bin/pkcs11-probe || exit 1'` and a note about testing on both SoftHSM and vendor HSMs.

maya: Added a Ruby SDK example for customers that need to present client certs to an egress TLS-terminating appliance and still proxy through an HTTP proxy (rare but we saw it). Ruby snippet: 

```ruby
require 'net/http'
uri = URI('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health')
proxy = Net::HTTP::Proxy('proxy.corp', 8080)
http = proxy.new(uri.host, uri.port)
http.use_ssl = true
http.cert = OpenSSL::X509::Certificate.new(File.read('/etc/redwood/certs/client.crt'))
http.key = OpenSSL::PKey::RSA.new(File.read('/etc/redwood/certs/client.key'))
resp = http.start { |h| h.get(uri.request_uri, { 'Authorization' => 'Bearer <KEY>' }) }
puts resp.code
```

ben: Nice. Tiny nit: call out Ruby >=2.6 and OpenSSL support.

docs-bot: Preview deployed for PR 4680 (:white_check_mark:)

oliver: Thanks all 44d I'll update the manifest section with sha256 verification `sha256sum -c images.manifest` and merge after the editorial pass.
